newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest, technical slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest, technical slide.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on seasonal harvest pressure and on a continuation of a longer-term technical slide, traders said.

Tuesday's USDA crop update showed the U.S. corn harvest at 20 pct, below expectations for 30 pct and down from the average 34 pct pace. But traders said damper weather this week in the U.S. Midwest would cause farmers to shift away from soybean combining to corn harvesting.
"Some viewed the 20 percent as bullish but others said the 80 percent of harvest still to come is bearish," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Technically the market remained in a downturn as Tuesday's close saw the the 20 day moving average for December at $299-1/4 and the four-day at $286-1/2 acting as bearish driving forces.

But the short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December at 21.55 points during Tuesday's close and 24.334 Wednesday, indicated an oversold scenario with an RSI of 20 or less considered a very oversold level by most technicians.
Corn closed 3/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/4 at $2.83-1/4.
The market was still reeling from Friday's bearish USDA crop production report and mostly routine export news.
USDA Wednesday said Egypt bought 500,000 tonnes of U.S. corn but traders said Egypt was expected to enter the U.S. corn market.

Key players included Merrill Lynch Futures with three million bushels sold in the December versus a purchase of two million, traders said. Refco Inc sold 1.5 million December and sold three million March and Cargill Investor Services sold three million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 40,000 contracts.
